lines.text: An estimated two to almost four million bitcoin are gone for good, because their keys were lost.
Stellar now holds nearly four billion dollars in tokenized assets, yet the inheritance tools built for Bitcoin and Ethereum don't work on Stellar.
This is Riktha. Name an heir for your Stellar account, and sign once.
Your heir doesn't need crypto. Just their email address.
Choose how long Riktha waits. Six months, a year, or exactly what you want.
Then you sign one transaction in Freighter. That's the whole setup.
From now on, you live normally. Every transaction you send resets the clock.
Go quiet for the whole window, and a claim starts. But you're warned long before it does.
By email, on Telegram, and on your dashboard. One transaction from you cancels the claim.

They open the link, type the six words you left them, and the account is theirs.
No wallet. No seed phrase. They send the funds anywhere, even straight to an exchange.

The network rejects them until you've been silent long enough. And anything you send uses up their sequence number, so they can never run.
Riktha never holds a key. The handover is enforced by the network, not by our servers.
